articles.title: Doorman Highlights Normalisation of Racial Abuse After Incident at Ko-Ko Lounge
articles.excerpt: Jawad Ali, a doorman at Ko-Ko Lounge in Rochdale, has raised concerns about the increasing normalisation of racial abuse following a recent incident involving a club-goer.
articles.content_html:
A doorman at Ko-Ko Lounge in Rochdale has raised concerns about the normalisation of racial abuse after witnessing a disturbing incident on Saturday night. Jawad Ali, 20, reported that a woman became aggressive and shouted racial slurs at a black security guard when asked to move away from an exit.

The incident, captured on video and shared widely online, shows the woman making derogatory gestures towards the guard. Ali, who was working for Protective One Security at the time, described the behaviour as "disgusting" and stated that he now expects such incidents during his shifts.

Greater Manchester Police confirmed they have received a report regarding the incident and are currently conducting inquiries. Ali alleged that the woman also directed racial abuse towards him before the video was recorded.

This incident raises significant concerns about the treatment of security staff and the prevalence of racial abuse in nightlife settings. As investigations continue, it highlights the need for greater awareness and action against such behaviour.

articles.title: Rochdale Borough Council Invites Feedback on Customer Access Strategy
articles.excerpt: Residents are encouraged to participate in the consultation regarding the proposed Customer Access & Experience Strategy, aimed at enhancing interactions with the Council over the next five years.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has launched a public consultation inviting residents to share their views on the proposed Customer Access & Experience Strategy for the next five years. This strategy aims to improve how residents contact the Council and receive support, ensuring a more consistent experience across various channels, including online, telephone, and face-to-face interactions.

The Council has identified six priorities for enhancing customer access and has outlined nine pledges detailing what residents can expect from its services. The intention is to simplify the process for residents seeking information, advice, and support, making it easier for them to navigate the Council's services without needing to understand its organisational structure.

The consultation is open to all residents, and the Council is eager to know if the proposed priorities and pledges resonate with the community or if there are any gaps that need addressing. The draft strategy, along with related documents such as an Equality Impact Assessment and a Sustainability Impact Assessment, is available for review on the Rochdale Borough Council Consultation Hub.

Residents interested in participating can find more information and submit their views through the Council's consultation page. The feedback period will help shape the final version of the strategy, ensuring it effectively meets the needs of the community.

articles.title: Martlet Kitchen at Rochdale Town Hall Wins Tripadvisor Travellers’ Choice Award 2026
articles.excerpt: The Martlet Kitchen, located in Rochdale Town Hall, has received the Tripadvisor Travellers’ Choice Award for 2026, recognising its commitment to quality and local sourcing.
articles.content_html:
The Martlet Kitchen, situated within Rochdale Town Hall, has been awarded the Tripadvisor Travellers’ Choice Award for 2026. This accolade places the restaurant among the top 10 percent of listings on the popular travel platform, highlighting its dedication to quality and customer satisfaction.

Chef Darren Parkinson, who has previously worked at renowned establishments such as Shibden Mill Inn and Fleece Inn, leads the kitchen at the Martlet Kitchen. The restaurant is known for its focus on British cuisine, sourcing ingredients from local suppliers to create a menu that is regularly updated. Notable dishes include fish and chips, and the restaurant also features a grill club on Fridays and fine dining on Saturday evenings.

Sarah Crabtree serves as the restaurant manager, overseeing a team that prides itself on delivering excellent service. The Martlet Kitchen also offers private dining options in the Mayor’s reception room, catering to various events and gatherings.

Darren Parkinson aims to achieve further accolades in the future, building on the restaurant's reputation for consistent positive reviews. The Martlet Kitchen's recognition by Tripadvisor underscores its commitment to providing a high-quality dining experience in a Grade I listed building.

articles.title: Chris Cheap Appointed Managing Director of Atom Valley’s Northern Gateway Regeneration
articles.excerpt: Chris Cheap has been appointed as the new managing director of the Atom Valley Northern Gateway Mayoral Development Corporation, overseeing significant regeneration projects in Rochdale and surrounding areas.
articles.content_html:
The Atom Valley Northern Gateway Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) has appointed Chris Cheap as its new managing director. This appointment is part of a broader initiative aimed at revitalising the Atom Valley area, which spans across Bury, Oldham, and Rochdale, focusing on advanced manufacturing, innovation, housing, and infrastructure.

The Northern Gateway is a pivotal component of the Atom Valley Mayoral Development Zone, which aims to drive economic growth and reindustrialisation in the region. Recently, the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC), a 30,000 sq ft facility located within the 25-acre Atom Valley Innovation District at Kingsway Park in Rochdale, was completed, marking an important step in the development.

One of the key projects under the Northern Gateway will enhance highway connections between the site and the M66 and M60 motorways. This improvement is essential for unlocking further phases of development and complements ongoing works to increase capacity at the nearby Simister Island.

Chris Cheap brings nearly 23 years of experience from Avison Young, where he held various leadership roles. His expertise will be crucial as the MDC seeks to implement its ambitious plans for the Northern Gateway, which is expected to play a significant role in the UK government's Northern Growth Strategy.

articles.title: Rochdale and Grimsby Town Share Points in 2-2 Draw at Crown Oil Arena
articles.excerpt: A late equaliser from Ian Henderson secured a point for Rochdale in a thrilling 2-2 draw against Grimsby Town in League Two on October 20, 2026.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC salvaged a point in a dramatic 2-2 draw against Grimsby Town at the Crown Oil Arena on Tuesday, October 20, 2026. The match saw veteran striker Ian Henderson come off the bench to score an equaliser in the 88th minute, preventing Grimsby from claiming all three points after they had taken the lead in the second half.

The game began with both teams eager to break their recent poor form. Rochdale took the lead in the 38th minute when Dajaune Brown scored following a well-placed cross from Glenn Middleton. However, Grimsby responded strongly after the break, with Kieran Green equalising in the 57th minute after a saved header from Andy Cook. The visitors then took the lead in the 72nd minute through Jamie Walker, who capitalised on a partially cleared corner.

Despite trailing, Rochdale continued to press for a goal. Their persistence paid off when Henderson, who had been introduced as a substitute, headed in a cross from Charlie Tasker to level the score just before full-time. This late goal marked a significant moment for Rochdale, who had recently suffered a defeat against Crewe Alexandra, ending a five-match unbeaten run.

The draw leaves Rochdale in 13th place in League Two with 15 points, while Grimsby Town, who ended a four-match losing streak, sit just behind in 15th with 14 points. Both teams will look to build on this result in their upcoming fixtures as they aim to improve their standings in the league.

articles.title: Rochdale House Prices Rise to £211,000 in August 2026
articles.excerpt: The average house price in Rochdale increased by 3.3% over the past year, while private rents saw a significant rise of 8.8%, according to the latest figures from the Office for National Statistics.
articles.content_html:
The average house price in Rochdale reached £211,000 in August 2026, reflecting a 3.3% increase from the previous year, according to data released by the Office for National Statistics (ONS). This rise is notably higher than the average increase of 2.2% observed across the North West during the same period.

In addition to house prices, private rents in Rochdale also saw a substantial increase, with the average rent climbing to £859 in September 2026. This marks an annual rise of 8.8%, compared to £790 in September 2025, again outpacing the North West's average increase of 5.7%.

For first-time buyers, the average price paid for a home was £191,000 in August 2026, which is a 3.4% increase from the previous year's average of £184,000. Homes purchased with a mortgage had an average price of £215,000, also reflecting a 3.3% rise from £208,000 in August 2025.

These figures indicate a continuing trend of rising housing costs in Rochdale, which may impact affordability for local residents. The ONS advises that local housing data can be more variable due to the smaller number of properties involved, and they recommend looking at trends over a longer period for a clearer picture.

This forms part of a wider scheme to create a connection between the train station and the town centre. ‌ The wider regeneration of the area around Rochdale railway station also involves the creation of a new public square in front of the station and 33 new apartments on a brownfield site on the corner of Maclure Road and Station Road. ‌ Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The train station in Rochdale was once a hub for industrial business generations ago, so the distance between the station and the town centre was purposeful separation. But as times changed, society changed and the station suddenly started transporting people, not goods. This is why there is an idea to improve access and avenues from the station and the main hub of the town. This 81-home development, known as John Rennie Place, in honour of the late Scottish Civil engineer who masterminded the Rochdale Canal, got under way in November last year, and is due for completion in December 2027. ‌ View 4 Images The former Central Retail Park site development under construction (Image: Rochdale council) The project, approved years ago, was unlocked following a successful bid for £15m from the government’s Community Regeneration Partnerships Fund. The transformation has been on the cards for a long time, but the local authority struggled to get the investment until last year. ‌ The properties will be the first affordable net zero homes delivered as part of a housing scheme supported by the council. The local authority says the development is already delivering benefits to the local economy and community. Contractor Willmott Dixon, working on behalf of the council, has already spent £3.3m with local civil engineering firm, Hovington Ltd, and supported a total of 95 weeks of apprenticeship and T-Level training, including three T-Level placements from Hopwood Hall College. ‌ Don't let an algorithm decide what Manchester news you see - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Seven local people are also employed on the project, including two people who were previously unemployed, with the council’s work and skills team supporting the recruitment. ‌ Tommy Patterson, 22, from Middleton , is one of the local people working on the new homes. He said: “I had been out of work for six months when the job centre arranged for me to get my CSCS card and that led to me securing a scaffolding apprenticeship here on site. I have always worked and had been let go, so getting this job was a lifeline. “I live on my own and I was struggling to pay my bills. It’s great to work here. Everyone is lovely; it’s a smashing team.” ‌ View 4 Images Councillor Danny Meredith looking across the former Rochdale Central Retail Park site (Image: Rochdale council) Daniel Fletcher, 17, is studying for a T Level in design, surveying and planning at Hopwood Hall College, said: “I really like it here. I’ve been talking to the different trades delivering this project, so I’ve been exposed to different parts of the job, and I have the freedom to go onto site on my own. articles.title: Plans Submitted for Demolition of Seven Blocks on Lower Falinge Estate in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has submitted plans to demolish seven blocks on the Lower Falinge Estate to make way for 270 new homes, aiming to improve living conditions in the area.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has submitted plans to Rochdale Council for the demolition of seven blocks on the Lower Falinge Estate, with the aim of constructing 270 new homes. The blocks earmarked for demolition include Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, Zedburgh, and Vaynor, which have been identified as no longer providing safe and warm living conditions.

The proposed redevelopment will primarily take place on land adjacent to Sheriff Street and Falinge Road, with additional plots near Redcross Street also included in the plans. RBH has indicated that the new homes will be a mix of houses and flats, all available for social rent, and designed to meet modern energy efficiency standards.

The plans come after a previous attempt to demolish the blocks was halted by a legal challenge from residents, who argued that there was no clear regeneration plan following the demolition. However, RBH has now provided a detailed regeneration strategy, which includes creating new landscaping, public open spaces, and safer streets, as well as improved walking routes into Rochdale town centre.

One resident, Andy Roche, who currently occupies Zedburgh, expressed distress over the plans, stating that he feels the needs of residents have not been adequately considered. Despite being offered alternative housing options, he claims none meet his current living standards. RBH has stated that they have engaged with local residents and stakeholders to ensure the new homes reflect community priorities.
